vectorGuide.why: Why it matters on the table

rise.what: Radial deviation of the wrist — bending the hand toward the thumb so the knuckles stay the highest point of the contact.
rise.why: A high knuckle line dictates the geometry of the match. Whoever controls knuckle height dictates the angle everyone else has to fight from.
rise.how: Train with a thick-bar wrist roller, static strap riser holds (3 × 20–30 s), and hammer-curl-to-radial-deviation supersets twice a week. Keep elbow stacked under the shoulder; let the wrist do the work, not the bicep.
rise.mistakes: Recruiting the bicep to "lift" the wrist (it rotates, it doesn't rise), letting the elbow drift out, and training with the palm flat on the table (this trains nothing).
rise.cue: Knuckles up. Elbow in. Wrist does the work.

cup.what: Wrist flexion — closing the hand into a deep C-shape so your palm wraps over the back of your own thumb and covers the opponent's fingers.
cup.why: The cup is inside position. It controls depth, denies the opponent knuckle access, and sets up every finish: toproll, hook, or press.
cup.how: Cup holds on a cable column with 60–80% 1RM (4 × 15 s), wrist-curl machines with full range, and heavy hammer curls to thicken the flexor mass. Pull against a strap fixed to a table for table-specific timing.
cup.mistakes: Shallow cup (fingers straight = no depth), cupping with the fingers only instead of the whole palm, and forgetting to drive the cup with shoulder pressure — a cup without pressure is just a hand shape.
cup.cue: Deep palm, fingers over their thumb. Drive it with your shoulder.

pronation.what: Rotating the forearm so the palm turns face-down at the contact — the "crack."
pronation.why: Pronation nullifies an opponent's cup, exposes their wrist, and converts your structure into a descending force they have to absorb with bone, not muscle.
pronation.how: Pronator curls (seated, elbow on knee) 4 × 8–12, reverse wrist curls with a light bar, and table-specific pronation holds on a fixed strap. Heavy single-rep pronation lifts with a partner beat the central nervous system into the pattern.
pronation.mistakes: Pronating with the wrist instead of the forearm (loses power), pronating before you have inside position (sliding on top of their cup), and training it without a strap — air-pronation builds nothing.
pronation.cue: Turn the key, don't twist the doorknob. Forearm rotates, palm goes down.

supination.what: Rotating the forearm palm-up — the entry to the hook and the recovery after a lost toproll.
supination.why: Supination is the transition. It's what lets you shift from a toproll that's stalled into a hook that's pulling. Without it you only have one gear.
supination.how: Hammer curls with thick handles, reverse-grip cable rows, and slow supination reps with a light dumbbell (3 × 12 each side). Practice the supination-to-curl chain on a strap twice a week.
supination.mistakes: Using supination to "escape" a strong toproll (you're moving backward, not transitioning), and dropping the elbow when you supinate — the elbow must stay pinned or the hook has no root.
supination.cue: Palm up, elbow in, shoulder pulls. That's the hook.

side.what: Lateral force applied to the opponent's hand and wrist toward their pinky side, combined with elbow placement that drives your shoulder into the contact line.
side.why: Side pressure bends the opponent's structure sideways, separates their shoulder from their hand, and creates the angle for a clean pin or a transition to a press.
side.how: Side-press holds on a cable stack with 70% load (4 × 12 s), landmine press rotations, and table-specific side-pressure drills where a partner resists your lateral push.
side.mistakes: Pushing with the arm instead of driving from the hip/shoulder, elbow flaring out to 90° (it should stay under the shoulder), and forgetting to pronate as you push side — side without pronation slides off.
side.cue: Drive from the hip, elbow under shoulder, pronate as you push.

back.what: Posterior chain force — pulling with the lats, teres, and rear delt to drag the opponent's arm across your body toward your chest.
back.why: Back pressure is the engine of the pull. No amount of wrist technique moves a heavy arm without it. It's also the most tendon-friendly force vector because the load travels through bone, not joint capsule.
back.how: Heavy rows (Pendlay, barbell, or single-arm dumbbell) 4 × 5–8, face pulls with high reps, and deadlifts to build the posterior chain. On the table, practice the "shoulder to pocket" cue — drag the strap toward your chest pocket.
back.mistakes: Pulling with the biceps (they're not built for it, your tendons will tell you), losing elbow position when you pull, and forgetting to engage the lat before the arm fires.
back.cue: Shoulder to pocket. Lat first, hand second.

rules.title: Rules quick reference
rules.subtitle: WAF-style table rules
rules.disclaimer: Always check your specific federation's rulebook — details vary.
rules.setup1: Shoulders parallel to the table; starting grip is set by the referee, grip must be closed with thumb visible.
rules.setup2: Wrists must be straight at start; neither competitor may bend before "Go".
rules.setup3: Free hand grips the peg at all times during the match.
rules.setup4: Elbow must stay on the pad — leaving it is a foul.
rules.cmd1: "Ready… Go" — do not move before "Go" (false start = warning/foul).
rules.cmd2: After a slip or foul, competitors re-grip; repeated slips can cost the round.
rules.cmd3: "Stop" freezes the match instantly — release pressure immediately.
rules.cmd4: The referee calls the pin; keep pulling until you hear it.
rules.foul1: False start or lifting your elbow off the pad.
rules.foul2: Intentionally slipping your grip to reset (often = loss of the round).
rules.foul3: Opening your hand or releasing the peg.
rules.foul4: Two fouls usually lose the round; severe fouls can end the match.
rules.strap1: If grips keep slipping, the referee straps wrists together.
rules.strap2: Once strapped, grip cannot slip — position battles decide it.
rules.strap3: Strap rules differ between federations; learn yours.
rules.win1: Pin = pressing the opponent's hand until their wrist/pin-pad touches within the pin zone (~45°).
rules.win2: Most matches are best of 3 rounds.
rules.win3: A pinned wrist held flat for the count wins even from a defensive position.
rules.cond1: No abusive language or unsportsmanlike behavior — instant warnings or DQ.
rules.cond2: Respect the referee's calls; appeals go through your captain only.
rules.cond3: Show up weighed-in and on time — missed weigh-in = disqualification.

wristRiserRoller.name: Thick-bar wrist roller riser
wristRiserRoller.step1: Forearms supported, thick handle in hand, elbow pinned.
wristRiserRoller.step2: Roll up, then raise knuckles to the top and pause 2–3 s.
wristRiserRoller.cue: Knuckles highest point — let the wrist lift, not the biceps.

cupHoldCable.name: Cable cup hold
cupHoldCable.step1: Rope/cone attached low-to-mid pulley; deep C-cup grip.
cupHoldCable.step2: Stand tall, hold the cup under tension 15–20 s.
cupHoldCable.step3: Drive the cup with shoulder pressure, not fingers alone.
cupHoldCable.cue: Deep palm over the thumb — pressure from the shoulder.

pronationLiftStrap.name: Strap pronation lift
pronationLiftStrap.step1: Seated, elbow on knee, strap wrapped around hand.
pronationLiftStrap.step2: Rotate palm down from neutral without moving the elbow.
pronationLiftStrap.cue: The forearm rotates; the wrist just follows.

slowSupination.name: Slow dumbbell supination
slowSupination.step1: Light dumbbell, elbow tucked at your side.
slowSupination.step2: Rotate palm-up over 3–4 s down, control back.
slowSupination.cue: Elbow pinned — rotation comes from the forearm only.

sidePressCable.name: Side-press cable hold
sidePressCable.step1: Cable at chest height behind you; hand stacked over wrist.
sidePressCable.step2: Press laterally toward the pinky side, elbow under shoulder.
sidePressCable.cue: Drive from hip and shoulder — pronate as you push.

heavyRows.name: Heavy rows (back pressure)
heavyRows.step1: Barbell or single-arm row, torso hinged.
heavyRows.step2: Drag the weight toward your chest pocket, lat-first.
heavyRows.cue: Lat fires before the hand moves.

hammerCurlMass.name: Hammer curls for flexor mass
hammerCurlMass.step2: Curl to shoulder height without swinging.
hammerCurlMass.cue: Thick forearms win long matches — feed the flexors.

multispinnerToproll.name: Multi-spinner toproll work
multispinnerToproll.step1: Load spinner, cup the handle deep.
multispinnerToproll.step2: Crack wrist then climb knuckles over the top.
multispinnerToproll.step3: Finish with back-pressure drag to the chest.
multispinnerToproll.cue: Cup → rise → drag: one continuous chain.

staticStrapHold.name: Static strap riser hold
staticStrapHold.step1: Fixed strap at table height, wrist fully risen.

partnerTablePulls.name: Partner table pulls
partnerTablePulls.step1: Grip up at the table with a partner resisting.
partnerTablePulls.step2: Hit your A-game entry 8× per side, submaximal.
partnerTablePulls.step3: Rotate positions: cup, side press, toproll finish.
partnerTablePulls.cue: Table time beats gym time — drill positions, not loads.
